Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The first discovery set gives three robust findings and many mostly null driver associations. H6 is accepted: MSI-high lines have much stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low lines. The signed estimate +0.789 for direction -1 means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is about -0.789, i.e. MSI-high cells are far more negative/dependent; the 95% interval entirely excludes zero and is huge relative to WRN's score distribution. H7 is accepted: SMARCA4-loss lines show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact lines, again a very large raw negative shift with a tight interval excluding zero. H8 is rejected in the registered direction because the interval strongly indicates the opposite relationship: KEAP1-loss lines have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. This is scientifically plausible because KEAP1 loss activates NRF2/NFE2L2 pathway signaling, potentially reducing the incremental effect of knocking out NFE2L2 itself, but the registered claim was the opposite direction, so the claim itself must be rejected and a reversed comparison registered. H3 EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency is the most useful validation target: the signed estimate +0.0252 is about a 10% shift relative to the average absolute EGFR dependency score, but the interval is borderline near zero, so I leave it unresolved and request independent validation. H1 KRAS is borderline and unresolved: the signed point estimate is positive and supports the hypothesized stronger KRAS dependency, but the interval includes zero and only partly includes clinically meaningful magnitude, so it is too weak to accept. I keep it active for subgroup refinement. H2, H9, and H12 are rejected for the registered direction because their intervals do not support a meaningful effect in the anticipated direction; in H2 and H12 the upper bound for hypothesis-supporting magnitude is below about 10% of the score distribution, and in H9 the maximum hypothesis-supporting effect is also below the approximate 10% threshold. H4, H5, H10, and H11 remain unresolved but not promising: their intervals include either null or clinically meaningful effects in both directions or only weak support, so I do not accept them and close them to current follow-up unless a stronger marker or interaction emerges. Overall, the evidence best supports WRN/MSI, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 inverse association, while classical RTK driver-biomarker associations in this dataset are weak or borderline.

record.narrative:
The requested independent validation resolves H3 against the EGFR-amplification dependency hypothesis. The discovery evidence R3 pointed weakly toward stronger EGFR dependency in EGFR-amplified lines (signed estimate +0.025 relative to the registered negative direction), but its interval crossed zero and only barely included a roughly 10% clinically meaningful shift. The validation evidence R13, reported with a much more conservative independent interval, had the opposite signed point estimate (-0.022), with an interval from about -0.064 to +0.019. Its upper bound for the registered hypothesis direction is below the approximate 0.025 clinical-magnitude threshold, while the point estimate and interval are compatible with no effect or the opposite direction. Thus the original global claim that EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency is not supported and is rejected. This does not establish causality or generalizability; it only means this dataset does not support the registered association. I still keep an interaction refinement to ask whether a small adenocarcinoma-restricted effect exists, but the main EGFR-amplification claim should not be accepted.

The strongest current dataset-supported findings are: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; and KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H13 should now be accepted. Its evidence R8, when signed to the reversed +1 direction, gives a very large positive contrast (about +0.80) with a very tight interval excluding zero. Biologically, KEAP1 loss activates NRF2/NFE2L2 pathway output, which could plausibly reduce the incremental fitness effect of NFE2L2 knockout, yielding weaker NFE2L2 dependency scores in KEAP1-loss cells. This remains an association in this supplied dataset, not proof of mechanism or external generalizability.

For next analyses, I will prioritize ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency because SWI/SNF paralog relationships are mechanistically parallel to the SMARCA4-loss finding. I will also test whether KRAS and EGFR effects are restricted to adenocarcinoma using both subgroup estimates and interactions. To avoid over-interpreting null driver-biomarker associations, I add a technical library-control comparison using Avana library exposure and dependency_POLR2A; if library exposure shifts POLR2A by a meaningful amount, that will help interpret whether technical variation contributes to null biological associations.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The current dataset-supported associations are unusually large for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, and weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1 loss. The next explore stage focuses on whether these are context-robust associations or reflections of co-mutation, subtype, proliferation state, or screen artifacts. I add refinements that isolate SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact cells and ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells to test whether SMARCA2 dependency is specific to SMARCA4 loss or reflects broader SWI/SNF lesions. Similarly, I test KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact cells and STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells because KEAP1 and STK11 often co-occur in lung adenocarcinoma models; this distinguishes a KEAP1/NRF2 association from a co-mutational marker effect. For WRN, I test whether the MSI-high effect remains in adenocarcinoma and across fast-growing and slower-growing cultures, since replication-stress dependencies can be proliferation-dependent. I also refine the null MYC-amplification/RPL11 claim by restricting to cells with high MYC expression, a marker-quality test for whether the binary amplification call is biologically informative when transcriptional MYC output is also high. Finally, I add technical and negative-control probes: an Avana-library association for WRN and an association with a research marker that has no assigned biological role. These help detect whether broad screen variation or arbitrary assay associations could affect interpretation. These remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal claims or externally generalizable conclusions.

record.narrative: I am requesting the 12 analyses that best test whether the three strongest existing dataset associations are specific and robust rather than artifacts of co-mutation, subtype, growth state, random assay noise, or screen-library variation. For SMARCA2, H28 tests SMARCA4 loss while requiring ARID1A to be intact, H29 tests ARID1A loss while requiring SMARCA4 to be intact, H30 tests SMARCA4 loss within adenocarcinoma, and H31 tests SMARCA4 loss in faster-growing cultures. These distinguish paralog-specific SWI/SNF biology from a broad complex-deficient marker or context effect. For NFE2L2, H32 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact lines and H33 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact lines, which is important because KEAP1 and STK11 frequently co-occur in lung models and the accepted NFE2L2 association could be confounded by co-mutational state. For WRN, H34-H36 test the MSI-high association in adenocarcinoma, faster-growing lines, and slower-growing lines, checking whether the replication-stress dependency is subtype- and proliferation-robust. I also include H15 to follow up the borderline KRAS-mutation association in adenocarcinoma, where driver effects are most expected. Finally, H38 and H39 provide control analyses: H38 tests Avana-library exposure against the accepted WRN outcome, and H39 tests a research marker with no assigned biological role against the accepted SMARCA2 outcome. These controls help determine whether accepted large effects could be partly technical or whether an unexplained dataset structure could produce large marker-association contrasts.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
The new discovery set strongly reinforces the three largest accepted dataset associations and makes them more specific. H28/R14 shows that SMARCA4 loss is still associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency when restricted to ARID1A-intact cells; the signed estimate is about +0.777 for the negative dependency-direction claim, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is roughly -0.777. This is enormous relative to SMARCA2 score scale, so H28 is accepted. H29/R15 tests ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells and gives a tiny, direction-inconsistent contrast (signed -0.003), with a maximum hypothesis-supporting magnitude well below the approximate 10% SMARCA2 scale; H29 is rejected. Thus the SMARCA2 association looks much more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to ARID1A loss in this selected dataset.

H30 and H31 accept SMARCA4 loss within adenocarcinoma and faster-growing lines, respectively. These subgroup effects are nearly as large as the global effect, although H31 is restricted to measured growth-rate cases. H32/R18 accepts the co-mutation-isolated reversed NFE2L2 finding: among STK11-intact lines, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (signed +0.801 for the positive direction, i.e. less negative dependency). This is very large and supports specificity to KEAP1 rather than STK11. H33/R19 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact lines and is essentially null; because the NFE2L2 score distribution and registered direction make the exact 10% boundary somewhat sensitive, I leave H33 unresolved but closed as not promising. I request independent validation of H32 because it is a refined, biologically important reversal claim and is well powered.

record.narrative:
The independent validation of H32 is decisive and strengthens the accepted KEAP1-loss association for weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H32 asks whether, among STK11-intact lines, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast because less negative dependency means weaker dependency. The discovery evidence R18 gave a signed estimate of +0.801 with a 95% interval from about +0.779 to +0.823. The new independent validation R26 is even stronger: signed estimate +0.815, with a very conservative independent interval from +0.782 to +0.847. Both estimates are far above the approximate clinically meaningful magnitude threshold for this outcome distribution and exclude zero decisively. Therefore H32 is accepted and its investigation can be closed. The result remains an association in this supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as proof of causality or external generalizability, but it is among the most robust dataset-supported findings here.

The overall supported evidence now centers on three biological associations. First, MSI-high lines have much stronger WRN dependency. The global H6 estimate is about +0.790 signed toward stronger dependency, with interval +0.760 to +0.819. This is robust in adenocarcinoma, faster-growing lines, and slower-growing lines, with H34, H35, and H36 all giving very large lower bounds. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The global H7 estimate is about +0.784 signed toward stronger dependency, interval +0.765 to +0.803, and it remains large when restricted to ARID1A-intact lines, adenocarcinoma, and faster-growing lines. ARID1A loss in SMARCA4-intact lines is essentially null, so the SMARCA2 finding is more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to SWI/SNF lesions generally in this dataset. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The reversed H13 claim is supported globally, and the validated co-mutation-isolated H32 claim is now strongly supported. STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact lines is not meaningfully associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, helping distinguish KEAP1 from STK11 co-mutational confounding.

Negative findings are also informative. The global EGFR-amplification claim H3 was rejected after discovery plus independent validation; the validated interval favored no effect or the opposite direction. BRAF V600E to stronger BRAF dependency H2, KRAS mutation to RIT1 dependency H9, and MYC amplification to stronger RPL11 dependency H12 were also rejected for the registered direction. Control comparisons suggest that the large accepted effects are not explained by the tested arbitrary assay or the tested positive Avana-library direction: marker E was not associated with SMARCA2 in a clinically meaningful way, and Avana exposure was not associated with stronger WRN dependency, though a modest inverse library association remains possible. 

Important uncertainty remains. KRAS-mutation association with KRAS dependency is weak globally and in adenocarcinoma; the intervals include both null and clinically meaningful effects, so it remains unresolved. Many broader pathway and marker hypotheses remain untested or only partially tested, including EGFR adenocarcinoma-specific and interaction claims, STAT3 and TMED10 associations with RTK amplifications, MYC-related DHX9 and POLR2A claims, ARID1A broad claim H14, WRN BRCA2 claim, RIT1 NF1 claim, the POLR2A library control, and high-MYC-expression RPL11 refinement. The next most informative analyses should combine these pending broad comparisons with newly registered robustness tests for the accepted effects: higher screen-quality restriction and Avana-library subsets for WRN/SMARCA2/NFE2L2 associations, plus co-loss probes for KEAP1 with STK11 and SMARCA4 with ARID1A. These will clarify whether the large accepted effects persist under technical-quality restriction and how much they depend on co-occurring genomic alterations.

Next analyze should run pending pathway/interaction claims and new robustness/co-loss proposals.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The current dataset-supported associations are unusually large for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, and weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1 loss. The next explore stage focuses on whether these are context-robust associations or reflections of co-mutation, subtype, proliferation state, or screen artifacts. I add refinements that isolate SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact cells and ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells to test whether SMARCA2 dependency is specific to SMARCA4 loss or reflects broader SWI/SNF lesions. Similarly, I test KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact cells and STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells because KEAP1 and STK11 often co-occur in lung adenocarcinoma models; this distinguishes a KEAP1/NRF2 association from a co-mutational marker effect. For WRN, I test whether the MSI-high effect remains in adenocarcinoma and across fast-growing and slower-growing cultures, since replication-stress dependencies can be proliferation-dependent. I also refine the null MYC-amplification/RPL11 claim by restricting to cells with high MYC expression, a marker-quality test for whether the binary amplification call is biologically informative when transcriptional MYC output is also high. Finally, I add technical and negative-control probes: an Avana-library association for WRN and an association with a research marker that has no assigned biological role. These help detect whether broad screen variation or arbitrary assay associations could affect interpretation. These remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal claims or externally generalizable conclusions.","analyze":"I am requesting the 12 analyses that best test whether the three strongest existing dataset associations are specific and robust rather than artifacts of co-mutation, subtype, growth state, random assay noise, or screen-library variation. For SMARCA2, H28 tests SMARCA4 loss while requiring ARID1A to be intact, H29 tests ARID1A loss while requiring SMARCA4 to be intact, H30 tests SMARCA4 loss within adenocarcinoma, and H31 tests SMARCA4 loss in faster-growing cultures. These distinguish paralog-specific SWI/SNF biology from a broad complex-deficient marker or context effect. For NFE2L2, H32 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact lines and H33 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact lines, which is important because KEAP1 and STK11 frequently co-occur in lung models and the accepted NFE2L2 association could be confounded by co-mutational state. For WRN, H34-H36 test the MSI-high association in adenocarcinoma, faster-growing lines, and slower-growing lines, checking whether the replication-stress dependency is subtype- and proliferation-robust. I also include H15 to follow up the borderline KRAS-mutation association in adenocarcinoma, where driver effects are most expected. Finally, H38 and H39 provide control analyses: H38 tests Avana-library exposure against the accepted WRN outcome, and H39 tests a research marker with no assigned biological role against the accepted SMARCA2 outcome. These controls help determine whether accepted large effects could be partly technical or whether an unexplained dataset structure could produce large marker-association contrasts.","appraise":"The new discovery set strongly reinforces the three largest accepted dataset associations and makes them more specific. H28/R14 shows that SMARCA4 loss is still associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency when restricted to ARID1A-intact cells; the signed estimate is about +0.777 for the negative dependency-direction claim, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is roughly -0.777. This is enormous relative to SMARCA2 score scale, so H28 is accepted. H29/R15 tests ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells and gives a tiny, direction-inconsistent contrast (signed -0.003), with a maximum hypothesis-supporting magnitude well below the approximate 10% SMARCA2 scale; H29 is rejected. Thus the SMARCA2 association looks much more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to ARID1A loss in this selected dataset.\n\nH30 and H31 accept SMARCA4 loss within adenocarcinoma and faster-growing lines, respectively. These subgroup effects are nearly as large as the global effect, although H31 is restricted to measured growth-rate cases. H32/R18 accepts the co-mutation-isolated reversed NFE2L2 finding: among STK11-intact lines, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (signed +0.801 for the positive direction, i.e. less negative dependency). This is very large and supports specificity to KEAP1 rather than STK11. H33/R19 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact lines and is essentially null; because the NFE2L2 score distribution and registered direction make the exact 10% boundary somewhat sensitive, I leave H33 unresolved but closed as not promising. I request independent validation of H32 because it is a refined, biologically important reversal claim and is well powered.\n\nH34, H35, and H36 accept MSI-high versus WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma, faster-growing lines, and slower-growing lines, respectively. The lower bounds remain far above clinical-magnitude thresholds, even though H36 has a smaller exposed cell (25) and wider interval. The MSI-high WRN association appears robust across available subtype and growth-rate contexts. H15/R23 remains unresolved: KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma lines show a weak positive signed contrast consistent with stronger KRAS dependency, but the interval includes both null and clinically meaningful effects; this is not enough to accept.\n\nThe control probes are reassuring but not absolutely perfect. H38/R24 tests Avana-library exposure for WRN in the registered positive direction; the signed estimate is negative and the upper bound for a positive library effect is below the approximate 10% WRN threshold, so the registered positive association is rejected. A modest inverse library association is not excluded, but it is small relative to the accepted MSI-high effect. H39/R25 tests an arbitrary research marker against SMARCA2; no clinically meaningful positive contrast is present, supporting that the SMARCA2 finding is not driven by an unassigned binary assay. Overall, the evidence now supports co-mutation-isolated and context-robust dataset associations for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and MSI-high/WRN, with strong dataset support for KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 that is pending independent validation.","synthesize":"The independent validation of H32 is decisive and strengthens the accepted KEAP1-loss association for weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H32 asks whether, among STK11-intact lines, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast because less negative dependency means weaker dependency. The discovery evidence R18 gave a signed estimate of +0.801 with a 95% interval from about +0.779 to +0.823. The new independent validation R26 is even stronger: signed estimate +0.815, with a very conservative independent interval from +0.782 to +0.847. Both estimates are far above the approximate clinically meaningful magnitude threshold for this outcome distribution and exclude zero decisively. Therefore H32 is accepted and its investigation can be closed. The result remains an association in this supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as proof of causality or external generalizability, but it is among the most robust dataset-supported findings here.\n\nThe overall supported evidence now centers on three biological associations. First, MSI-high lines have much stronger WRN dependency. The global H6 estimate is about +0.790 signed toward stronger dependency, with interval +0.760 to +0.819. This is robust in adenocarcinoma, faster-growing lines, and slower-growing lines, with H34, H35, and H36 all giving very large lower bounds. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The global H7 estimate is about +0.784 signed toward stronger dependency, interval +0.765 to +0.803, and it remains large when restricted to ARID1A-intact lines, adenocarcinoma, and faster-growing lines. ARID1A loss in SMARCA4-intact lines is essentially null, so the SMARCA2 finding is more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to SWI/SNF lesions generally in this dataset. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The reversed H13 claim is supported globally, and the validated co-mutation-isolated H32 claim is now strongly supported. record.narrative:
The new robustness and co-mutation analyses further strengthen the three largest dataset-supported associations while providing useful negative controls. For WRN/MSI-high, H43/R27 shows that the association remains extremely large under stricter screen-quality restriction, with signed estimate about +0.795 and lower bound +0.758, far above the approximate 10% WRN clinical-magnitude threshold around +0.03. H50/R30 shows the same near-global effect under matched RNA/DNA availability, with lower bound about +0.760. These results support accepting H43 and H50 and closing them as accepted context-robust refinements. For SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, H52/R31 shows the effect remains huge under matched RNA/DNA availability, lower bound about +0.760, far above the approximate SMARCA2 threshold around +0.04. H49/R29 is especially informative because it tests SMARCA4 loss specifically among ARID1A-loss lines: the signed effect is about +0.814 with lower bound +0.767, indicating the association is not weakened when SWI/SNF co-loss is present. This is a strong new accepted refinement, but because the exposed cell is small (n=76) and this is a newly accepted claim, I request independent validation of H49. For NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, H48/R28 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines and gives a very large positive signed effect, lower bound +0.727, far above the small NFE2L2 absolute-scale clinical threshold around +0.009. This complements the already validated STK11-intact H32 result and supports that the KEAP1 association is not limited to one co-mutational stratum.

The negative and borderline claims are mostly unhelpful. H57/R33 tests PIK3CA mutation for stronger STAT3 dependency; the signed estimate is opposite the registered direction and the upper bound for hypothesis-supporting effect is well below the approximate STAT3 threshold, so H57 is rejected. H60/R35 tests NF1 loss among KRAS-wildtype lines for stronger RIT1 dependency; the registered positive-support interval does not reach the RIT1 clinical threshold, so H60 is rejected. H61/R36 is a useful negative control using research marker D against WRN; the upper positive bound is far below the WRN threshold, supporting that arbitrary binary assay structure does not reproduce the large MSI-high effect. H56/R32 remains unresolved but closed: RB1 loss shows a small positive point estimate for WRN dependency, but the interval includes null and some clinically meaningful values, while the point estimate is not compelling. H59/R34 also remains unresolved but closed: KRAS-mutant TP53-intact lines show a small positive signed effect for KRAS dependency, but the interval includes null and values above threshold; this is not enough to accept. H16/R37 is a borderline EGFR-amplification subgroup test: it remains unresolved but closed because the point estimate is below threshold and the global EGFR claim was already independently rejected; H37/R38 similarly remains unresolved but closed because the estimate is essentially null despite an interval that barely includes clinically meaningful positive effects. Overall, the evidence continues to support WRN dependence in MSI-high lines, SMARCA2 dependence in SMARCA4-loss lines, and weaker NFE2L2 dependence in KEAP1-loss lines, with these findings remaining dataset-specific associations rather than causal or generalizable claims.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

record.narrative:
The newly released validation for H28 and H49 decisively confirms the SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss association as the second major dataset-supported finding after WRN/MSI-high, while the H3 validation response resolves the EGFR-amplification claim against the registered stronger-dependency hypothesis.

First, H3 asked whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency, direction -1. Discovery R3 gave a signed estimate of about +0.025 with interval from about -0.000 to +0.051. This was near the approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean EGFR score threshold around +0.025, but the interval included null and could not support acceptance. The independent validation R13 is now available and is signed opposite the registered stronger-dependency direction: estimate about -0.022, interval about -0.064 to +0.019. The upper bound of the hypothesis-supporting interval is below the approximate clinical-magnitude threshold of +0.025 and the point estimate favors the opposite direction, i.e. weaker EGFR dependency with EGFR amplification. H3 is therefore rejected and closed. I registered a reversal proposal for weaker EGFR dependency with EGFR amplification because the validated data suggest that possibility, but the reversal interval still includes null and the discovery point estimate favored the opposite direction, so it remains unresolved and should not be accepted.

Second, H28 tested SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact lines for stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R14 gave signed estimate +0.777 with lower bound +0.756; independent validation R40 gives estimate +0.812 with lower bound +0.778. These are vastly larger than the approximate SMARCA2 meaningful threshold around +0.042. H28 is accepted and closed. This shows that the strong SMARCA4-loss effect is not explained by ARID1A-intact selection alone; it remains enormous even when ARID1A loss is excluded.

Third, H49 tested the complementary co-loss situation: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines for stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R29 gave signed estimate +0.814 with lower bound +0.767; independent validation R39 gives estimate +0.811 with lower bound +0.743. This again far exceeds the approximate SMARCA2 clinical threshold. H49 is accepted and closed. Together with H7, H28, H30, H31, and H52, the evidence supports that SMARCA2 dependency is strongly and specifically associated with SMARCA4 loss, regardless of ARID1A status. The ARID1A-only effect among SMARCA4-intact lines (H29/R15) remains null, reinforcing that ARID1A loss alone is not the driver.

The broader evidence now supports three main dataset-specific associations:
1. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. The global H6 estimate is signed +0.790 with lower bound +0.760; this is far above the approximate WRN threshold around +0.030. It remains robust in adenocarcinoma, faster and slower growth strata, higher screen-quality restriction, and matched RNA/DNA subsets.
2. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Global H7 is signed +0.784, lower bound +0.765, and validations/subgroup restrictions remain far above threshold.
3. KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The reversed global claim H13/R8 is signed +0.796, and the validated STK11-intact H32/R18/R26 is signed about +0.80 to +0.81. H48/R28 shows the same large weaker-dependency association among STK11-loss lines, with lower bound +0.727. This effect is therefore co-mutation robust in this dataset.

Negative findings are also useful. EGFR amplification is not supported for stronger EGFR dependency after validation. BRAF V600E for stronger BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation for stronger RIT1 dependency, MYC amplification for stronger RPL11 dependency, PIK3CA mutation for stronger STAT3 dependency, and NF1 loss among KRAS-wildtype lines for stronger RIT1 dependency are rejected for the registered directions. ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact lines is essentially null. Control tests with research markers and Avana-library positive-direction hypotheses have not produced clinically meaningful effects comparable to the accepted associations, although library and assay negative controls are not exhaustive.

Important uncertainty remains. KRAS mutation effects on KRAS dependency are weak globally and in adenocarcinoma; I have marked H1/H15 deferred as low-priority unresolved claims unless future interaction or quality-restricted tests change that assessment. The possible opposite EGFR-amplification/weaker EGFR dependency association remains unresolved and was formally registered. Broad untested associations still include ARID1A global SMARCA2, STAT3/TMED10 with RTK amplifications, MYC-related DHX9/POLR2A/USP7/KIF18A effects, WRN/BRCA2, RIT1/NF1 global, lineage interactions, and library/low-serum robustness tests.

The most informative next analysis should prioritize: formal interaction and within-stratum co-loss tests for the accepted associations, especially SMARCA4 x ARID1A and KEAP1 x STK11 specificity; the EGFR reversal claim; remaining broad untested pathway associations; and matched-direction research-marker controls. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied lung-cell-line dataset, not causal effects or generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Next analyze should prioritize interaction/co-loss specificity, EGFR reversal, broad untested claims, and controls.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The registered new comparisons keep the focus on both robustness of the strongest dataset-supported associations and expansion into untested predictors. For WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, and KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency, I add reliability and context restrictions: matched RNA/DNA availability and low-serum culture conditions. These probe whether the very large associations persist when genomic calls may be better supported and under a simpler culture condition. For accepted associations, I explicitly attach parent claims and available motivating evidence only where a parent has evidence. The broader set asks whether RB1 loss is associated with stronger WRN dependency, whether PIK3CA mutation has any association with STAT3 dependency, whether the weak EGFR/ERBB2 driver signals become informative in adenocarcinoma or after removing TP53 co-loss, and whether NF1 loss is associated with stronger RIT1 dependency after excluding KRAS-mutant lines. All hypotheses remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable conclusions.","analyze":"I am selecting 12 analyses that combine focused robustness/co-loss tests for the strongest accepted dataset associations with several high-value unresolved and negative-control probes. For WRN/MSI-high, H50 tests whether the large association persists when only matched RNA/DNA profiles are used, and H43 tests whether it remains under stricter screen-quality restriction using screen_roc_auc >= 0.95. These address whether the accepted WRN effect is stable under better genomic-call reliability and high-quality CRISPR screens. For SMARCA2, H52 tests the SMARCA4-loss effect under matched RNA/DNA availability, while H49 tests the complementary co-loss situation: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines. H49 is important because H28 showed the effect is strong when ARID1A is intact; H49 tests whether the association persists when the two SWI/SNF lesions co-occur. For NFE2L2, H48 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines, complementing the already validated H32 test among STK11-intact lines and helping determine whether the KEAP1 association is robust to STK11 co-loss rather than only an isolated co-mutational marker effect. The broad set then targets remaining unresolved driver and pathway questions: H16 asks whether EGFR amplification has an adenocarcinoma-specific association after the global EGFR claim was rejected; H59 asks whether KRAS-mutation dependency becomes clearer among TP53-intact lines, isolating the driver from a common co-loss; H60 asks whether NF1 loss is associated with stronger RIT1 dependency after excluding KRAS-mutant lines; H56 tests RB1 loss as another replication/cell-cycle-related predictor of WRN dependency; H57 tests PIK3CA mutation as a STAT3-pathway predictor; and H37 refines the MYC/RPL11 null by using high transcriptomic MYC rather than binary amplification. Finally, H61 is a negative control using research marker D against WRN, the same outcome as the accepted MSI-high effect, to assess whether an unassigned binary assay can produce a large positive contrast. This mix should either strengthen specificity of the accepted associations or reveal additional scientifically meaningful dataset associations, while keeping all conclusions limited to this supplied dataset.","appraise":"The new robustness and co-mutation analyses further strengthen the three largest dataset-supported associations while providing useful negative controls. For WRN/MSI-high, H43/R27 shows that the association remains extremely large under stricter screen-quality restriction, with signed estimate about +0.795 and lower bound +0.758, far above the approximate 10% WRN clinical-magnitude threshold around +0.03. H50/R30 shows the same near-global effect under matched RNA/DNA availability, with lower bound about +0.760. These results support accepting H43 and H50 and closing them as accepted context-robust refinements. For SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, H52/R31 shows the effect remains huge under matched RNA/DNA availability, lower bound about +0.760, far above the approximate SMARCA2 threshold around +0.04. H49/R29 is especially informative because it tests SMARCA4 loss specifically among ARID1A-loss lines: the signed effect is about +0.814 with lower bound +0.767, indicating the association is not weakened when SWI/SNF co-loss is present. This is a strong new accepted refinement, but because the exposed cell is small (n=76) and this is a newly accepted claim, I request independent validation of H49. For NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, H48/R28 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines and gives a very large positive signed effect, lower bound +0.727, far above the small NFE2L2 absolute-scale clinical threshold around +0.009. This complements the already validated STK11-intact H32 result and supports that the KEAP1 association is not limited to one co-mutational stratum.\n\nThe negative and borderline claims are mostly unhelpful. H57/R33 tests PIK3CA mutation for stronger STAT3 dependency; the signed estimate is opposite the registered direction and the upper bound for hypothesis-supporting effect is well below the approximate STAT3 threshold, so H57 is rejected. H60/R35 tests NF1 loss among KRAS-wildtype lines for stronger RIT1 dependency; the registered positive-support interval does not reach the RIT1 clinical threshold, so H60 is rejected. H61/R36 is a useful negative control using research marker D against WRN; the upper positive bound is far below the WRN threshold, supporting that arbitrary binary assay structure does not reproduce the large MSI-high effect. H56/R32 remains unresolved but closed: RB1 loss shows a small positive point estimate for WRN dependency, but the interval includes null and some clinically meaningful values, while the point estimate is not compelling. H59/R34 also remains unresolved but closed: KRAS-mutant TP53-intact lines show a small positive signed effect for KRAS dependency, but the interval includes null and values above threshold; this is not enough to accept. H16/R37 is a borderline EGFR-amplification subgroup test: it remains unresolved but closed because the point estimate is below threshold and the global EGFR claim was already independently rejected; H37/R38 similarly remains unresolved but closed because the estimate is essentially null despite an interval that barely includes clinically meaningful positive effects. Overall, the evidence continues to support WRN dependence in MSI-high lines, SMARCA2 dependence in SMARCA4-loss lines, and weaker NFE2L2 dependence in KEAP1-loss lines, with these findings remaining dataset-specific associations rather than causal or generalizable claims.","synthesize":"The newly released validation for H28 and H49 decisively confirms the SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss association as the second major dataset-supported finding after WRN/MSI-high, while the H3 validation response resolves the EGFR-amplification claim against the registered stronger-dependency hypothesis.\n\nFirst, H3 asked whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency, direction -1. Discovery R3 gave a signed estimate of about +0.025 with interval from about -0.000 to +0.051. This was near the approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean EGFR score threshold around +0.025, but the interval included null and could not support acceptance. The independent validation R13 is now available and is signed opposite the registered stronger-dependency direction: estimate about -0.022, interval about -0.064 to +0.019. The upper bound of the hypothesis-supporting interval is below the approximate clinical-magnitude threshold of +0.025 and the point estimate favors the opposite direction, i.e. weaker EGFR dependency with EGFR amplification. H3 is therefore rejected and closed. I registered a reversal proposal for weaker EGFR dependency with EGFR amplification because the validated data suggest that possibility, but the reversal interval still includes null and the discovery point estimate favored the opposite direction, so it remains unresolved and should not be accepted.\n\nSecond, H28 tested SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact lines for stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R14 gave signed estimate +0.777 with lower bound +0.756; independent validation R40 gives estimate +0.812 with lower bound +0.778. These are vastly larger than the approximate SMARCA2 meaningful threshold around +0.042. H28 is accepted and closed. This shows that the strong SMARCA4-loss effect is not explained by ARID1A-intact selection alone; it remains enormous even when ARID1A loss is excluded.\n\nThird, H49 tested the complementary co-loss situation: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines for stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R29 gave signed estimate +0.814 with lower bound +0.767; independent validation R39 gives estimate +0.811 with lower bound +0.743. This again far exceeds the approximate SMARCA2 clinical threshold. H49 is accepted and closed. Together with H7, H28, H30, H31, and H52, the evidence supports that SMARCA2 dependency is strongly and specifically associated with SMARCA4 loss, regardless of ARID1A status. The ARID1A-only effect among SMARCA4-intact lines (H29/R15) remains null, reinforcing that ARID1A loss alone is not the driver.\n\nThe broader evidence now supports three main dataset-specific associations:\n1. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. The global H6 estimate is signed +0.790 with lower bound +0.760; this is far above the approximate WRN threshold around +0.030. record.narrative: The next comparisons are designed to test whether the large accepted dataset associations are robust to technical and biological context, and whether less-resolved driver/pathway claims become clearer after co-alteration or transcriptomic filtering. For the three accepted effects, I registered stricter context tests: high mutation burden for WRN/MSI-high to probe whether the association is merely a generic high-mutation-burden artifact; Ky-library subsets to test whether the associations survive an alternative CRISPR screening platform rather than being specific to the dominant Avana library; and very high screen ROC for SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss and NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, paralleling the already accepted high-quality-screen restriction for WRN. Persistence under these conditions would strengthen confidence that these are not technical artifacts, while attenuation would suggest quality- or library-dependent associations. For pathway isolation, I registered EGFR-amplification-negative ERBB2 and ERBB2-amplification-negative EGFR comparisons, with the EGFR claim in the weaker-dependency direction suggested by prior validation, to assess whether RTK amplification effects are diluted by co-amplification. I also registered KRAS-mutation dependency under high screen quality, TP53-loss MDM2 dependency among CDKN2A-intact lines, and BRAF-mutant RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype lines. Finally, because binary MYC amplification was globally near-null for several MYC-related dependencies, I registered MYC-amplification tests restricted to high transcriptomic MYC expression, where amplification is more likely to be transcriptionally active. All claims remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable effects.

Interpretations remain dataset-specific associations.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The next comparisons are designed to test whether the large accepted dataset associations are robust to technical and biological context, and whether less-resolved driver/pathway claims become clearer after co-alteration or transcriptomic filtering. For the three accepted effects, I registered stricter context tests: high mutation burden for WRN/MSI-high to probe whether the association is merely a generic high-mutation-burden artifact; Ky-library subsets to test whether the associations survive an alternative CRISPR screening platform rather than being specific to the dominant Avana library; and very high screen ROC for SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss and NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, paralleling the already accepted high-quality-screen restriction for WRN. Persistence under these conditions would strengthen confidence that these are not technical artifacts, while attenuation would suggest quality- or library-dependent associations. For pathway isolation, I registered EGFR-amplification-negative ERBB2 and ERBB2-amplification-negative EGFR comparisons, with the EGFR claim in the weaker-dependency direction suggested by prior validation, to assess whether RTK amplification effects are diluted by co-amplification. record.narrative: The new robustness analyses strongly support the three major dataset-specific associations and do not materially change their interpretation. Approximate 10% relative thresholds based on population absolute means are about +0.030 for WRN, +0.042 for SMARCA2, +0.009 for NFE2L2, +0.025 for EGFR, +0.026 for ERBB2, +0.026 for RIT1, and +0.018 for USP7. For WRN/MSI-high, H69/R41 in high-mutation-burden lines gives a signed effect +0.782 with lower bound +0.749, and H70/R42 in the alternative KY library gives +0.732 with lower bound +0.675. Both intervals are far above the WRN clinical-magnitude threshold and far from null. H69 therefore addresses the concern that MSI-high is merely a generic high-TMB marker: the WRN association persists among lines selected for relatively high mutation burden. H70 addresses platform specificity: the association is still enormous in KY, despite the exposed cell having only 32 lines. These accept H69 and H70 as robust dataset-specific refinements, though I note the small exposed cell in H70 and rely on the consistency with the global effect and many prior strata. For SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, H71/R43 under very high screen-quality restriction and H72/R44 in KY both yield huge positive signed effects (+0.793 and +0.816) with lower bounds above +0.75. These are well above the approximate SMARCA2 threshold and support accepting both as robust dataset-specific refinements. For NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, H73/R45 under very high screen-quality restriction and H74/R46 in KY both yield very large weaker-dependency effects (+0.797 and +0.794) with lower bounds above +0.75. These are far above the small NFE2L2 absolute-mean threshold and support accepting both. Together, H69-H74 strengthen the core triad against mutation-burden, screen-quality, and library-platform concerns. The interaction results are much less informative. H64/R47 asks whether the SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 differs by ARID1A loss; the interaction is +0.037 with interval -0.015 to +0.089. This is near the SMARCA2 threshold but includes null and cannot establish meaningful effect modification. Given the already accepted within-stratum effects in ARID1A-intact and ARID1A-loss groups, I leave it unresolved and closed. H66/R48 asks whether the KEAP1-loss effect on NFE2L2 differs by STK11 loss; the interaction is -0.026 with interval -0.079 to +0.026. It includes null and supports neither a clinically meaningful enhancement nor attenuation in the registered direction, so it remains unresolved and closed. RTK isolation tests are mostly null. H75/R49 tests stronger ERBB2 dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines and gives a near-zero estimate +0.001 with interval -0.028 to +0.030. Because the interval includes null and clinically meaningful positive values, H75 is unresolved but closed. H76/R50 tests weaker EGFR dependency among ERBB2-amplification-negative lines and gives signed estimate -0.027 with interval -0.053 to -0.001. For the registered weaker-dependency direction, this interval is entirely opposite the hypothesis, so H76 is rejected. It does suggest the opposite possibility that EGFR amplification may be associated with stronger EGFR dependency when ERBB2 amplification is absent, but the opposite-direction interval after sign reversal would only barely clear null and not robustly clear threshold, so I registered a new unresolved refinement rather than accepting it. H79/R51 tests BRAF V600E stronger RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype lines; the signed point estimate is negative and the upper bound +0.021 is below the approximate RIT1 threshold +0.026. The interval does not support a clinically meaningful RIT1-dependency increase, so H79 is rejected and closed. H82/R52 tests MYC amplification stronger USP7 dependency among high MYC-expression lines. The signed point estimate +0.029 is above the approximate USP7 threshold +0.018, but the interval -0.037 to +0.095 is wide, includes null, and includes clinically meaningful opposite values. There is not enough evidence to accept or reject clinically meaningful USP7 association, so H82 remains unresolved and closed. I request independent validation of H6, the original global WRN/MSI-high association, because WRN is the largest accepted dataset-specific association and, unlike SMARCA2 and NFE2L2, it has not yet received independent validation. If validation remains large and positive, it will substantially strengthen confidence that the WRN/MSI-high finding is not a discovery-set artifact. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal claims or generalizable biology.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

All interpretations remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The next comparisons are designed to test whether the large accepted dataset associations are robust to technical and biological context, and whether less-resolved driver/pathway claims become clearer after co-alteration or transcriptomic filtering. For the three accepted effects, I registered stricter context tests: high mutation burden for WRN/MSI-high to probe whether the association is merely a generic high-mutation-burden artifact; Ky-library subsets to test whether the associations survive an alternative CRISPR screening platform rather than being specific to the dominant Avana library; and very high screen ROC for SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss and NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss, paralleling the already accepted high-quality-screen restriction for WRN. Persistence under these conditions would strengthen confidence that these are not technical artifacts, while attenuation would suggest quality- or library-dependent associations. For pathway isolation, I registered EGFR-amplification-negative ERBB2 and ERBB2-amplification-negative EGFR comparisons, with the EGFR claim in the weaker-dependency direction suggested by prior validation, to assess whether RTK amplification effects are diluted by co-amplification. Iteration 5/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score).
