Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
Final synthesis report.

Due assessments. For H112 (PTEN loss versus PTEN-intact within PIK3CA-intact and TP53-intact lines), discovery R70 estimated a clinically strong PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency, +0.293 with 95% Welch interval +0.228 to +0.358. The independent response deadline result R79 was +0.236 with stringent interval +0.140 to +0.332, cells 160 versus 1153. Against the approximate 10-percent threshold for dependency_STAT3 of about +0.028, the validation lower bound is about five times that threshold and clearly excludes both null and subclinical magnitudes. I therefore accept H112 as a supplied-dataset association and close the investigation.

For H37 (MYC-amplified lines with high MYC expression versus non-MYC-amplified high-MYC-expression lines on RPL11), discovery R38 was essentially null, and independent validation R80 gave a signed estimate -0.035 with interval -0.080 to +0.009. The relevant positive threshold for stronger dependency in this direction is about +0.025. The upper bound is below that threshold, and the interval includes no meaningful evidence of stronger RPL11 dependency in the claimed direction. This rejects the MYC-program/RPL11 association in the supplied dataset; I keep the investigation closed.

For H161 (CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact within TP53-loss lines on MDM2 dependency), discovery R95 was +0.111 with interval +0.035 to +0.186, cells 81 versus 325, above the approximate MDM2 threshold of +0.027. New independent validation R106 was +0.115 with stringent interval +0.002 to +0.227, cells 95 versus 310. Validation confirms direction and excludes zero under the stringent validation criterion, but its lower bound is near zero and below the 10-percent clinical threshold. Thus the TP53-loss-specific magnitude is less certain than the global CDKN2A/MDM2 association. I accept H161 as a dataset-specific association based on discovery plus consistent validation, but keep the investigation active because independent evidence alone does not establish a clinically meaningful effect size within TP53-loss cells. This is not a causal or generalizable claim.

Supported findings. The supplied lung cell-line dataset now supports five robust marker-dependency axes, all as associations rather than causal dependencies: MSI-high is associated with far stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss is associated with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, including in ARID1A-intact, ARID1A-loss, adenocarcinoma, CDKN2A-intact, and other marker-intact contexts; KEAP1 loss is associated with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, globally and in PIK3CA-intact/TP53-intact lines; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency globally, in clean TP53/PTEN/MSI-intact lines, in higher screen-quality or Cas9-quality contexts, and with positive but somewhat less certain magnitude in TP53-loss lines.

Negative or non-supported findings. Broad driver-gene dependency hypotheses were largely not supported. BRAF V600E did not show a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect. EGFR amplification did not show a robust stronger EGFR dependency effect globally; the only borderline signal was in ERBB2-intact lines, where the interval still included subthreshold values and the claim remains unresolved. ERBB2 amplification did not show a robust ERBB2 dependency effect. KRAS mutation, NF1 loss, STK11 loss, and PTEN loss were not accepted as markers of clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. MYC-amplification with high MYC expression was not associated with stronger RPL11 dependency, as now confirmed by validation. Many interaction tests did not support lineage subtype, KRAS status, PTEN/PIK3CA, TP53, or library status as effect modifiers, although several remain unresolved because intervals are wide rather than decisively negative.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main remaining scientific uncertainties are: whether CDKN2A-associated MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss lines is a clinically meaningful effect or a smaller effect that discovery overestimated; whether CDKN2A loss is specific to MDM2 relative to USP7, KRAS, STAT3, WRN, or SMARCA2 outcomes; and whether the borderline ERBB2-intact EGFR signal is real or noise. Assay-quality and lineage modifiers remain mostly unsupported but not fully excluded where intervals include clinically meaningful values. All conclusions remain limited to the supplied dataset and do not establish causal CRISPR dependency relationships or external generalizability.

Most informative next analyses. The registered refinements now target the CDKN2A/MDM2 axis: high screen-quality TP53-loss lines, PIK3CA-intact TP53-loss lines, adenocarcinoma TP53-loss lines, CDKN2A loss on USP7 within TP53-loss lines as a specificity control, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 in low-MYC-expression lines. These should clarify whether the TP53-loss attenuation concern is biological, whether the effect is context-specific, and whether the association is specific to MDM2 rather than part of a broader dependency phenotype.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

expectation

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The current evidence base supports five dataset-specific marker-dependency associations: MSI-high with far stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The next scientifically useful step is not to re-open accepted large-effect axes unless needed for marker independence, but to characterize the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis and to test two remaining driver-gene borderline signals. For CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, I register robustness and specificity refinements. Screen-batch interaction asks whether the effect is batch-specific; the KY-library mean difference asks whether it persists outside the dominant Avana library; slow-growth, high-MYC-expression, and KRAS-intact contexts ask whether the association is modified by proliferation state, transcriptional MYC program, or KRAS co-alteration. Because global CDKN2A-loss may correlate with other accepted marker losses, I also register specificity probes: in MSI-intact lines, PTEN-intact lines, SMARCA4-intact lines, and a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, test CDKN2A loss on WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and USP7 respectively. Positive signed estimates for direction -1 would mean stronger dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines. If upper bounds fall below the approximate 10-percent thresholds, these probes reject clinically meaningful cross-marker effects and support CDKN2A/MDM2 specificity; if lower bounds exceed the thresholds, CDKN2A loss should be interpreted as part of a broader dependency phenotype rather than an MDM2-specific marker. For the TP53-loss uncertainty around CDKN2A/MDM2, I register a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding MSI, KEAP1, and PTEN alterations. This should help determine whether the TP53-loss-specific effect remains above the MDM2 threshold or only weakly excludes null. Finally, I register context refinements for unresolved driver-gene hypotheses: EGFR amplification in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the borderline ERBB2-intact EGFR signal; and KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the absence of a global KRAS-mutation effect. For dependency outcomes, a more negative score is stronger dependency. Direction -1 hypotheses encode stronger dependency in the exposed group as raw negative contrasts, displayed as positive signed evidence. Interpretation remains association-only in the supplied lung cell-line dataset and does not imply causality or external generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

Do not infer causality or generalizability.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The current evidence base supports five dataset-specific marker-dependency associations: MSI-high with far stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The next scientifically useful step is not to re-open accepted large-effect axes unless needed for marker independence, but to characterize the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis and to test two remaining driver-gene borderline signals. For CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, I register robustness and specificity refinements. Screen-batch interaction asks whether the effect is batch-specific; the KY-library mean difference asks whether it persists outside the dominant Avana library; slow-growth, high-MYC-expression, and KRAS-intact contexts ask whether the association is modified by proliferation state, transcriptional MYC program, or KRAS co-alteration. Because global CDKN2A-loss may correlate with other accepted marker losses, I also register specificity probes: in MSI-intact lines, PTEN-intact lines, SMARCA4-intact lines, and a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, test CDKN2A loss on WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and USP7 respectively. Positive signed estimates for direction -1 would mean stronger dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines. If upper bounds fall below the approximate 10-percent thresholds, these probes reject clinically meaningful cross-marker effects and support CDKN2A/MDM2 specificity; if lower bounds exceed the thresholds, CDKN2A loss should be interpreted as part of a broader dependency phenotype rather than an MDM2-specific marker. For the TP53-loss uncertainty around CDKN2A/MDM2, I register a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding MSI, KEAP1, and PTEN alterations. This should help determine whether the TP53-loss-specific effect remains above the MDM2 threshold or only weakly excludes null. Finally, I register context refinements for unresolved driver-gene hypotheses: EGFR amplification in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the borderline ERBB2-intact EGFR signal; and KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the absence of a global KRAS-mutation effect. H167 asks whether it persists in TP53-loss lines within high-quality screens, which is important because the global p53 pathway signal could contribute to the MDM2 association. H183 asks whether the association remains in a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding PTEN loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high, thereby reducing possible confounding by other accepted marker-dependency axes. H175, H173, H174, and H176 test robustness to MYC-high expression, KY-library context, slower proliferation context, and KRAS-intact context. H177 through H180 are specificity controls for the CDKN2A axis: CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact on USP7 in a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. For these direction -1 specificity tests, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines; clinically meaningful effects in any of these outcomes would weaken a claim that CDKN2A loss is specific to MDM2 dependency. H181 follows up the unresolved EGFR-amplification signal in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines. All analyses use the standard 95% Welch tests with a minimum of 20 observations per comparison cell. Interpretation will use approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the clinical-significance threshold, for example about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.025 for EGFR. Estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be multiplied by direction again. I defer batch interaction, low-MYC expression, additional TP53-loss subgroup refinements, and KRAS-mutation refinement to later rounds because the current 12 slots are best spent on the new CDKN2A/MDM2 robustness and specificity question plus one driver-gene follow-up. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not imply causality or external generalizability.","appraise":"I audited the twelve newly delivered discovery comparisons using approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the dataset-specific clinical-significance benchmark. That lower bound is about three times the approximate MDM2 threshold of +0.027, so I accept H148 as a supplied-dataset association, not as a causal or generalizable claim. H161 tests the same CDKN2A/MDM2 contrast restricted to TP53-loss lines, where the prior pathway confounding concern is greatest. For CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, I register robustness and specificity refinements. Screen-batch interaction asks whether the effect is batch-specific; the KY-library mean difference asks whether it persists outside the dominant Avana library; slow-growth, high-MYC-expression, and KRAS-intact contexts ask whether the association is modified by proliferation state, transcriptional MYC program, or KRAS co-alteration. Because global CDKN2A-loss may correlate with other accepted marker losses, I also register specificity probes: in MSI-intact lines, PTEN-intact lines, SMARCA4-intact lines, and a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, test CDKN2A loss on WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and USP7 respectively. H167 asks whether it persists in TP53-loss lines within high-quality screens, which is important because the global p53 pathway signal could contribute to the MDM2 association. H183 asks whether the association remains in a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding PTEN loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high, thereby reducing possible confounding by other accepted marker-dependency axes. H175, H173, H174, and H176 test robustness to MYC-high expression, KY-library context, slower proliferation context, and KRAS-intact context. H177 through H180 are specificity controls for the CDKN2A axis: CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact on USP7 in a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. Interpretation will use approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the clinical-significance threshold, for example about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.025 for EGFR. For the MDM2 stress tests, H167, H175, H173, H174, and H176 have signed point estimates and lower confidence bounds well above the MDM2 threshold (R108 +0.140, lower +0.045; R110 +0.102, lower +0.040; R111 +0.116, lower +0.047; R112 +0.152, lower +0.075; R113 +0.101, lower +0.062). These are not causal claims, but they are dataset-specific associations and are robust in high-screen-quality, high-MYC-expression, KY-library, slow-growth, and KRAS-intact contexts, so I accept them and close further work. H164 is a high-screen-quality global context with R107 +0.090 but lower bound +0.022, which crosses the +0.027 clinical threshold; the point is clinically meaningful but the interval does not establish a clinically meaningful effect in that selected context with sufficient certainty, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. Do not interpret any finding as causal or generalizable.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The current evidence base supports five dataset-specific marker-dependency associations: MSI-high with far stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The next scientifically useful step is not to re-open accepted large-effect axes unless needed for marker independence, but to characterize the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis and to test two remaining driver-gene borderline signals. For CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, I register robustness and specificity refinements. Screen-batch interaction asks whether the effect is batch-specific; the KY-library mean difference asks whether it persists outside the dominant Avana library; slow-growth, high-MYC-expression, and KRAS-intact contexts ask whether the association is modified by proliferation state, transcriptional MYC program, or KRAS co-alteration. Because global CDKN2A-loss may correlate with other accepted marker losses, I also register specificity probes: in MSI-intact lines, PTEN-intact lines, SMARCA4-intact lines, and a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, test CDKN2A loss on WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and USP7 respectively. If upper bounds fall below the approximate 10-percent thresholds, these probes reject clinically meaningful cross-marker effects and support CDKN2A/MDM2 specificity; if lower bounds exceed the thresholds, CDKN2A loss should be interpreted as part of a broader dependency phenotype rather than an MDM2-specific marker. For the TP53-loss uncertainty around CDKN2A/MDM2, I register a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding MSI, KEAP1, and PTEN alterations. H167 asks whether it persists in TP53-loss lines within high-quality screens, which is important because the global p53 pathway signal could contribute to the MDM2 association. H183 asks whether the association remains in a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding PTEN loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high, thereby reducing possible confounding by other accepted marker-dependency axes. H175, H173, H174, and H176 test robustness to MYC-high expression, KY-library context, slower proliferation context, and KRAS-intact context. H177 through H180 are specificity controls for the CDKN2A axis: CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact on USP7 in a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. Interpretation will use approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the clinical-significance threshold, for example about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.025 for EGFR. Estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be multiplied by direction again. I defer batch interaction, low-MYC expression, additional TP53-loss subgroup refinements, and KRAS-mutation refinement to later rounds because the current 12 slots are best spent on the new CDKN2A/MDM2 robustness and specificity question plus one driver-gene follow-up. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not imply causality or external generalizability.","appraise":"I audited the twelve new discovery results using signed estimates and approximate 10% outcome-mean clinical-significance thresholds: MDM2 about +0.027, USP7 about +0.018, WRN about +0.030, STAT3 about +0.028, SMARCA2 about +0.042, EGFR about +0.025. For the MDM2 stress tests, H167, H175, H173, H174, and H176 have signed point estimates and lower confidence bounds well above the MDM2 threshold (R108 +0.140, lower +0.045; R110 +0.102, lower +0.040; R111 +0.116, lower +0.047; R112 +0.152, lower +0.075; R113 +0.101, lower +0.062). These are not causal claims, but they are dataset-specific associations and are robust in high-screen-quality, high-MYC-expression, KY-library, slow-growth, and KRAS-intact contexts, so I accept them and close further work. H164 is a high-screen-quality global context with R107 +0.090 but lower bound +0.022, which crosses the +0.027 clinical threshold; the point is clinically meaningful but the interval does not establish a clinically meaningful effect in that selected context with sufficient certainty, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. H183 is the cleanest TP53-loss specificity context (TP53 loss, MSI-intact, KEAP1-intact, PTEN-intact), with R109 +0.118 but lower bound +0.022, again just below threshold. Because this context directly addresses whether CDKN2A-associated MDM2 dependency remains clinically meaningful after excluding other accepted marker axes, I keep it active and request independent validation. The specificity probes were more informative: in MSI-intact lines, CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger WRN dependency (R115 +0.005, interval -0.014 to +0.025, below the +0.030 threshold in the claimed direction), so H178 rejects a clinically meaningful effect; in PTEN-intact lines CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (R116 -0.001, interval -0.022 to +0.020, below the +0.028 threshold), so H179 rejects a clinically meaningful effect; and in SMARCA4-intact lines CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (R117 +0.002, interval -0.022 to +0.026, far below the +0.042 threshold), so H180 rejects a clinically meaningful effect. H177 remains unresolved because the USP7 interval R114 +0.003, interval -0.025 to +0.031, spans the +0.018 threshold and therefore cannot rule out either stronger or weaker USP7 dependency at the clinical threshold, even though the point estimate is near null. H181 remains unresolved and deferred: the EGFR-amplification effect in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines is borderline (R118 +0.028) but the interval -0.001 to +0.057 includes null and subthreshold values, and the point estimate is unstable relative to the earlier ERBB2-intact test. All conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.","synthesize":"Final synthesis report.\n\nDue assessments. For H112 (PTEN loss versus PTEN-intact within PIK3CA-intact and TP53-intact lines), discovery R70 estimated a clinically strong PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency, +0.293 with 95% Welch interval +0.228 to +0.358. The independent response deadline result R79 was +0.236 with stringent interval +0.140 to +0.332, cells 160 versus 1153. Against the approximate 10-percent threshold for dependency_STAT3 of about +0.028, the validation lower bound is about five times that threshold and clearly excludes both null and subclinical magnitudes. I therefore accept H112 as a supplied-dataset association and close the investigation.\n\nFor H37 (MYC-amplified lines with high MYC expression versus non-MYC-amplified high-MYC-expression lines on RPL11), discovery R38 was essentially null, and independent validation R80 gave a signed estimate -0.035 with interval -0.080 to +0.009. The relevant positive threshold for stronger dependency in this direction is about +0.025. The upper bound is below that threshold, and the interval includes no meaningful evidence of stronger RPL11 dependency in the claimed direction. This rejects the MYC-program/RPL11 association in the supplied dataset; I keep the investigation closed.\n\nFor H161 (CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact within TP53-loss lines on MDM2 dependency), discovery R95 was +0.111 with interval +0.035 to +0.186, cells 81 versus 325, above the approximate MDM2 threshold of +0.027. New independent validation R106 was +0.115 with stringent interval +0.002 to +0.227, cells 95 versus 310. Validation confirms direction and excludes zero under the stringent validation criterion, but its lower bound is near zero and below the 10-percent clinical threshold. Thus the TP53-loss-specific magnitude is less certain than the global CDKN2A/MDM2 association. I accept H161 as a dataset-specific association based on discovery plus consistent validation, but keep the investigation active because independent evidence alone does not establish a clinically meaningful effect size within TP53-loss cells. This is not a causal or generalizable claim.\n\nSupported findings. The supplied lung cell-line dataset now supports five robust marker-dependency axes, all as associations rather than causal dependencies: MSI-high is associated with far stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss is associated with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, including in ARID1A-intact, ARID1A-loss, adenocarcinoma, CDKN2A-intact, and other marker-intact contexts; KEAP1 loss is associated with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, globally and in PIK3CA-intact/TP53-intact lines; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency globally, in clean TP53/PTEN/MSI-intact lines, in higher screen-quality or Cas9-quality contexts, and with positive but somewhat less certain magnitude in TP53-loss lines.\n\nNegative or non-supported findings. Broad driver-gene dependency hypotheses were largely not supported. BRAF V600E did not show a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect. EGFR amplification did not show a robust stronger EGFR dependency effect globally; the only borderline signal was in ERBB2-intact lines, where the interval still included subthreshold values and the claim remains unresolved. ERBB2 amplification did not show a robust ERBB2 dependency effect. KRAS mutation, NF1 loss, STK11 loss, and PTEN loss were not accepted as markers of clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. record.narrative: Due assessments. H146, global CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on dependency_MDM2, is accepted and closed. Discovery R92 estimated +0.117 with 95% Welch interval +0.082 to +0.152, and independent validation R93 estimated +0.114 with stringent interval +0.067 to +0.161. Against the approximate 10-percent MDM2 threshold of about +0.027, both discovery and validation lower bounds are well above the threshold. This supports a supplied-dataset association in which CDKN2A-loss lines show stronger MDM2 dependency. It is not a causal or external-generalizability claim. H183, CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on dependency_MDM2 within TP53-loss, MSI-intact, KEAP1-intact, PTEN-intact lines, is unresolved and remains active. Discovery R109 estimated +0.118 with interval +0.022 to +0.214, which excludes null but falls slightly below the clinical threshold at the lower bound. Independent validation R119 estimated a larger point difference, +0.165, but its stringent interval was -0.011 to +0.340 with cells 46 versus 203. Thus the clean TP53-loss context is direction-consistent but imprecise: it neither establishes a clinically meaningful effect nor excludes one. I do not accept H183 clinically, and I do not reject it because the interval includes large clinically meaningful positive magnitudes. This does not undermine the global CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; it indicates that the TP53-loss-specific clean context remains too uncertain for a clinically meaningful magnitude claim. Supported findings. The supplied lung cell-line dataset supports five main marker-dependency association axes: MSI-high is associated with far stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss is associated with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, including in PIK3CA-intact and TP53-intact lines; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The global CDKN2A-MDM2 association is now independently validated. Context robustness for CDKN2A-MDM2 is supported by several accepted mean differences, including high screen-quality contexts, high Cas9-activity contexts, high MYC expression, KY library, slow growth, KRAS-intact lines, clean TP53/PTEN/MSI-intact lines, TP53-loss high-screen-quality lines, and TP53-loss general MDM2 associations. These are dataset-specific associations and should be interpreted as robust measurement contexts, not biological mechanisms. Negative or non-supported findings. Broad driver-gene dependency hypotheses remain unsupported: BRAF V600E was not accepted as a marker of stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification was not accepted globally as a robust stronger EGFR dependency marker, and the borderline ERBB2-intact signal remains unresolved; ERBB2 amplification was not accepted as a stronger ERBB2 dependency marker; KRAS mutation, NF1 loss, STK11 loss, and PTEN loss were not accepted as markers of clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. MYC amplification with high MYC expression was not associated with stronger RPL11 dependency, and validation rejected the clinically meaningful claimed direction. CDKN2A-specificity probes rejected clinically meaningful cross-marker effects on WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines, supporting specificity of CDKN2A loss for MDM2 relative to those outcomes. Unresolved uncertainty. The principal unresolved question is whether CDKN2A loss is associated with clinically meaningful stronger MDM2 dependency specifically within TP53-loss lines. H161 remains accepted as a TP53-loss association, but its validation lower bound is near zero, and H183 remains unresolved after wide validation uncertainty. A second unresolved issue is USP7 specificity: cross-marker probes were reassuring for WRN, STAT3, and SMARCA2, but USP7 probes remain inconclusive, including the clean context H177 and the TP53-loss context H170. The borderline EGFR signal in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines remains unresolved and is not accepted as robust. Some lineage, assay-quality, and co-alteration modifiers remain unsupported because intervals are wide rather than decisively null. Next analyses. I registered three focused follow-ups: first, CDKN2A-MDM2 in a cleaner TP53-loss context restricted to higher screen ROC quality, to ask whether the H183 validation uncertainty is driven by imprecision in a small high-quality subset; second, CDKN2A-USP7 in TP53-loss higher-screen-quality lines, to reduce assay noise while probing USP7 specificity; third, a higher-screen-quality CDKN2A-by-TP53-loss interaction test on MDM2, to ask whether TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 association after restricting to more reliable screens. These are more informative than further broad driver-gene screening or repeated validation of already supported axes.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: These new proposals address three remaining gaps: a plausible p53/USP7 axis, proliferation-dependent MYC effects on transcription/R-loop/mitotic dependencies, RTK-amplification/secretory-trafficking effects in adenocarcinoma, and whether accepted marker-dependency axes are modified by TP53 status. The global TP53-loss to USP7 test is motivated by the MDM2-p53-USP7 deubiquitination axis: TP53-loss lines may need less USP7 to protect p53, giving weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. a less negative score and a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast encoded by direction +1. The MYC-by-high-proliferation tests ask whether MYC-amplified lines that are already dividing rapidly show stronger dependency on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9, as predicted by transcriptional stress, mitotic stress, and R-loop resolution demands; direction -1 encodes stronger dependency in MYC-amplified lines. The TMED10 tests probe EGFR or ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma because receptor tyrosine kinase signaling may increase secretory trafficking demand through TMED10; direction -1 again encodes stronger dependency. The RIT1 test examines EGFR amplification in KRAS-intact lines, where EGFR signaling through small RAS-family proteins might increase RIT1 dependency. Finally, the two interaction tests and the USP7/CDKN2A specificity control assess marker independence and context modification: whether TP53 loss modifies SMARCA4-loss or KEAP1-loss effects, and whether CDKN2A loss has a clean p53-wild-type, high-quality-screen USP7 effect. Clinical-significance thresholds remain approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean; for example USP7 about 0.018, POLR2A/KIF18A/DHX9/TMED10 about 0.025 to 0.026, and SMARCA2 about 0.042. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction and are dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: I request twelve existing active comparisons rather than retesting already resolved claims. The current priority is to interrogate the newly strengthened CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis for context modification and specificity, while keeping two useful breadth blocks. H187 tests whether TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency in the global population, a plausible p53/MDM2/USP7-axis extension. H170, H185, and H196 test CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on USP7 in TP53-loss general lines, TP53-loss high-screen-quality lines, and TP53-intact high-screen-quality lines, respectively; these distinguish whether any USP7 effect tracks TP53 loss, CDKN2A loss, screen quality, or neither. H186 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A-loss association with MDM2 dependency in higher-quality screens, which is important because H183 was directionally supportive but too imprecise and H167 was accepted only in a higher-quality TP53-loss context. For the breadth block, H188-H190 test whether MYC-amplified lines that are already proliferating rapidly show stronger transcription, mitotic, and R-loop-related dependencies on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9. H191 and H193 test receptor-tyrosine-kinase-associated secretory-trafficking and RIT1 hypotheses in focused genomic contexts. H194 and H195 test whether TP53 loss modifies two accepted axes: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency. I did not include H184 because it duplicates the already accepted H167 eligibility and comparison. Estimates, if returned, will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will be judged against approximate 10-percent absolute-outcome-mean thresholds: USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, POLR2A about 0.026, KIF18A about 0.026, DHX9 about 0.025, TMED10 about 0.025, RIT1 about 0.026, SMARCA2 about 0.042, and STAT3 about 0.028. I reassessed H161 to unresolved because the TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 discovery was clinically meaningful, but the independent validation had a very wide interval with lower bound near zero and below the clinical threshold; it is directionally supportive but cannot establish a clinically meaningful magnitude in that broad TP53-loss context. This does not challenge the global accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association. All requested analyses remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The main new finding is H187: TP53 loss versus intact is associated with a large signed positive mean difference in dependency_USP7 (R123 +0.396; 95% Welch interval +0.325 to +0.467; cells 406/1594). With direction +1, this means TP53-loss lines have higher, i.e. less negative, USP7 dependency scores than TP53-intact lines: weaker USP7 dependency. The interval is far above the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for USP7 (about +0.018), so I accept this as a dataset-specific association and request independent validation. I treat it as hypothesis-supporting evidence for a p53/USP7 axis, not proof of mechanism or external generalizability. Co-alteration confounding is plausible because TP53 loss is common and may correlate with other accepted markers, so I registered context and specificity tests: high-screen-quality TP53-loss, high-Cas9-activity TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact/high-screen-quality TP53-loss, and a TP53-by-CDKN2A interaction on USP7. The CDKN2A-USP7 probes H170, H185, and H196 remain unresolved because intervals are wide and span clinically meaningful positive and negative effects; they are deferred pending the TP53-specific follow-up. H186, the CDKN2A-by-TP53 interaction on MDM2 in higher-quality screens, is unresolved and deferred: it is conceptually important but too imprecise to accept or reject a clinically meaningful interaction. The MYC-amplification/fast-proliferation probes for POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and the intervals remain too wide for a clean null claim; because these were lower-prior broad hypotheses, I closed them without rejection. The TMED10 EGFR-amplification adenocarcinoma test and the EGFR-amplification RIT1 test in KRAS-intact lines are also unresolved closed because they are low-prior and not currently worth further allocation. The TP53 interaction tests for SMARCA4-SMARCA2 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 are deferred because the underlying axes are accepted and modification by TP53 status could matter, but the new intervals are imprecise and do not establish clinically meaningful interactions.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

All conclusions are dataset-specific associations, not causality or generalizability.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"These new proposals address three remaining gaps: a plausible p53/USP7 axis, proliferation-dependent MYC effects on transcription/R-loop/mitotic dependencies, RTK-amplification/secretory-trafficking effects in adenocarcinoma, and whether accepted marker-dependency axes are modified by TP53 status. The global TP53-loss to USP7 test is motivated by the MDM2-p53-USP7 deubiquitination axis: TP53-loss lines may need less USP7 to protect p53, giving weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. a less negative score and a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast encoded by direction +1. The MYC-by-high-proliferation tests ask whether MYC-amplified lines that are already dividing rapidly show stronger dependency on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9, as predicted by transcriptional stress, mitotic stress, and R-loop resolution demands; direction -1 encodes stronger dependency in MYC-amplified lines. The TMED10 tests probe EGFR or ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma because receptor tyrosine kinase signaling may increase secretory trafficking demand through TMED10; direction -1 again encodes stronger dependency. The RIT1 test examines EGFR amplification in KRAS-intact lines, where EGFR signaling through small RAS-family proteins might increase RIT1 dependency. Finally, the two interaction tests and the USP7/CDKN2A specificity control assess marker independence and context modification: whether TP53 loss modifies SMARCA4-loss or KEAP1-loss effects, and whether CDKN2A loss has a clean p53-wild-type, high-quality-screen USP7 effect. Clinical-significance thresholds remain approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean; for example USP7 about 0.018, POLR2A/KIF18A/DHX9/TMED10 about 0.025 to 0.026, and SMARCA2 about 0.042. H170, H185, and H196 test CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on USP7 in TP53-loss general lines, TP53-loss high-screen-quality lines, and TP53-intact high-screen-quality lines, respectively; these distinguish whether any USP7 effect tracks TP53 loss, CDKN2A loss, screen quality, or neither. H186 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A-loss association with MDM2 dependency in higher-quality screens, which is important because H183 was directionally supportive but too imprecise and H167 was accepted only in a higher-quality TP53-loss context. For the breadth block, H188-H190 test whether MYC-amplified lines that are already proliferating rapidly show stronger transcription, mitotic, and R-loop-related dependencies on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9. H191 and H193 test receptor-tyrosine-kinase-associated secretory-trafficking and RIT1 hypotheses in focused genomic contexts. H194 and H195 test whether TP53 loss modifies two accepted axes: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency. The interval is far above the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for USP7 (about +0.018), so I accept this as a dataset-specific association and request independent validation. I treat it as hypothesis-supporting evidence for a p53/USP7 axis, not proof of mechanism or external generalizability. Co-alteration confounding is plausible because TP53 loss is common and may correlate with other accepted markers, so I registered context and specificity tests: high-screen-quality TP53-loss, high-Cas9-activity TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact/high-screen-quality TP53-loss, and a TP53-by-CDKN2A interaction on USP7. The global TP53-loss to USP7 test is motivated by the MDM2-p53-USP7 deubiquitination axis: TP53-loss lines may need less USP7 to protect p53, giving weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. a less negative score and a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast encoded by direction +1. record.narrative: Independent validation is exhausted, so this exploration prioritizes precision, context, and specificity analyses around already supported dataset axes rather than broad driver screening. The highest-value open questions are: whether TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency is robust in high-Cas9, CDKN2A-intact and CDKN2A-loss strata and whether CDKN2A loss modifies the TP53 effect in higher-quality screens; whether CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency persists in TP53-loss/high-Cas9 contexts and also in TP53-intact/high-screen-quality contexts; whether PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency survives high screen quality and high Cas9 activity while holding CDKN2A intact; and whether the large accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-WRN, and SMARCA4-SMARCA2 associations remain clinically meaningful under combined high-screen-quality and CDKN2A-intact eligibility. Expected directions are: TP53 loss versus intact should give positive raw USP7 differences because TP53-loss lines show weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss versus intact should also give positive raw NFE2L2 differences because KEAP1-loss lines show weaker NFE2L2 dependency; CDKN2A loss, PTEN loss, MSI-high, and SMARCA4 loss versus their comparators should give negative raw differences because these markers are associated with stronger dependencies on MDM2, STAT3, WRN, and SMARCA2, respectively. The TP53-by-CDKN2A USP7 interaction is expected to be uncertain: independence would produce a small interaction, while pathway cooperation or confounding could produce a non-zero interaction. Clinical significance is judged against approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean thresholds, e.g. USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, STAT3 about 0.028, WRN about 0.030, SMARCA2 about 0.042, and NFE2L2 about 0.009. All claims are dataset-specific associations in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal mechanisms or external-generalizable conclusions.
